title: Judge leniency as IV for incarceration on recidivism

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
• Method: Two-Stage Least Squares (Instrumental Variables).  
• Instrument: “Judge leniency” (leave-one-out incarceration rate of the assigned judge).  
• Why IV? Assignment of cases to judges is as-good-as random, giving an exogenous source of variation in incarceration that is plausibly unrelated to defendants’ unobserved risk of re-offending.  
• Key assumptions  
 1. Relevance – judge leniency strongly predicts the incarceration decision (first-stage F > 10).  
 2. Exclusion – judge leniency affects recidivism only through its impact on incarceration, not through any other channel.  
 3. Independence – conditional on controls (offense type, priors, age) the instrument is independent of potential outcomes.  
 4. Monotonicity – no defendant would be less likely to be incarcerated when facing a stricter judge (no “defiers”).  

## 2. R Code
```r
#############################################
# Judge Leniency IV: Incarceration → Recidivism
#############################################

# Load packages ------------------------------------------------------------
pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest", "ivreg")
suppressPackageStartupMessages(invisible(lapply(pkgs, require, character.only = TRUE)))

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------------
file_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s23_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(file_path)

# Ensure correct types -----------------------------------------------------
df$y <- as.numeric(df$y)        # recidivism (0/1 or z-score)
df$x <- as.numeric(df$x)        # incarceration (0/1)
df$z <- as.numeric(df$z)        # judge leniency
df$controls <- as.numeric(df$controls)

# 2. First-stage regression -----------------------------------------------
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_summary <- coeftest(fs, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1"))
first_stage_F <- waldtest(fs, . ~ controls, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1"))$F[2]

# 3. 2SLS / IV estimation --------------------------------------------------
iv_mod <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1"))

# 4. Reduced form (for robustness) ----------------------------------------
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
rf_robust <- coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1"))

# 5. Alternative spec: no controls ----------------------------------------
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_noc_robust <- coeftest(iv_noc, vcov = vcovHC(iv_noc, type = "HC1"))

# 6. Print key numerical results ------------------------------------------
cat("\n================ First Stage =================\n")
print(fs_summary)
cat(sprintf("First-stage F-stat on instrument: %.2f\n", first_stage_F))

cat("\n================ 2SLS Main ====================\n")
print(iv_robust)

cat("\n============ Reduced Form (y~z) ===============\n")
print(rf_robust)

cat("\n========== 2SLS (No Controls) =================\n")
print(iv_noc_robust)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Theory and prior empirical work (e.g., “criminogenic” prison effects) suggest that incarceration is likely to *increase* the probability of subsequent offending. Accordingly, we expect:  
• Sign: positive IV coefficient on “x” (incarceration) in the second stage.  
• Magnitude: roughly 0.05–0.15 in probability terms (i.e., incarceration raises 3-year recidivism by 5–15 percentage points).  
• First-stage: instrument should be strong (F ≈ 30–100) given judges’ sizable variation in sentencing rates.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — judge leniency instrument; LATE for marginal defendants; test exclusion restriction carefully
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Incarceration increases recidivism for marginal defendants (criminogenic effect)
_ground_truth.main_effect: Incarceration raises 3-year recidivism probability by ~15pp for compliers
